body:
### Problem

An `nvim --embed` server whose UI goes away (e.g. the builtin TUI process is killed, the terminal window is closed) never exits if an error message is emitted while it is shutting down. It blocks forever in `wait_return()` waiting for `<Enter>` from a UI that no longer exists, and is left behind as an orphan process (reparented to PID 1). Any child processes of that server (`:terminal` jobs etc.) stay alive with it.

Sampled stack of such an orphan (macOS `sample`): `main → preserve_exit → getout → wait_return → … kevent`.

`getout()` has:

```c
  if (did_emsg) {
    // give the user a chance to read the (error) message
    no_wait_return = false;
    wait_return(false);
  }
```

and `wait_return()` only skips the prompt for `headless_mode && !ui_active()` (5b34c2a). A server that *had* a UI and lost it is not headless, so it blocks.

In my setup this happened at scale: a corrupt ShaDa file makes the ShaDa write at exit fail, so every nvim server whose TUI was closed stayed alive — 132 orphaned `nvim --embed` processes accumulated over a few days.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# needs tmux; uses an isolated XDG state dir
NVIM=${NVIM:-nvim}
T=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$T/state/nvim/shada"
printf 'x' > "$T/state/nvim/shada/main.shada"   # unparseable ShaDa -> E576 when nvim writes ShaDa at exit
tmux new-session -d -s nvimrepro -x 120 -y 30 -e XDG_STATE_HOME="$T/state" -e XDG_DATA_HOME="$T/data" -e XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$T/cfg" "$NVIM -u NORC"
sleep 3
tui=$(tmux display-message -p -t nvimrepro '#{pane_pid}')
embed=$(pgrep -P "$tui" -f 'nvim.*--embed' | head -1)
tmux kill-session -t nvimrepro      # TUI dies -> server loses its UI and begins to exit
sleep 4
if kill -0 "$embed" 2>/dev/null; then echo "BUG: nvim --embed $embed still alive, ppid $(ps -o ppid= -p $embed)"; kill -9 "$embed"; else echo "OK: server exited"; fi
rm -rf "$T"
```

Output: `BUG: nvim --embed 87213 still alive, ppid 1`.

The 1-byte ShaDa file is just a convenient way to get an error message *during* shutdown (`E576: Error while reading ShaDa file: expected positive integer at position 1, but got nothing`, raised when the exit-time ShaDa write reads the old file to merge). Any other error at that point should do the same.

### Expected behavior

With no UI attached there is nobody who can press `<Enter>`; the server should not block on the hit-enter prompt and should exit.

Changing `wait_return()` to return early whenever `!ui_active()` (not only in headless mode) fixes it — verified on master 4b26a2a: unpatched build hangs, patched build exits, in the script above. I'll open a PR.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.12.5 (Homebrew); also reproduced on master NVIM v0.13.0-dev-4b26a2a built from source

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

N/A (`--embed` / RPC UI is Nvim-specific)

### Operating system/version

macOS 27.0 (Apple Silicon)

### Terminal name/version

tmux 3.7c (inside iTerm2)

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-256color

### Installation

Homebrew (0.12.5); source build (master)

comment_data.body: PR: #42098. It limits the change to the exit path (`!ui_active() && (headless_mode || exiting)`) rather than any time no UI is attached as I first suggested above, so servers temporarily without a UI (e.g. after `:detach`) keep their current behaviour.

title: embedded server never exits after its UI is gone if an error occurs at exit (blocks in wait_return with no UI)
